A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GrACE research. The text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original confidence-calibration and test-time-scaling experiments, cross-domain evaluations, ablations, and a qualitative case study.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports confidence-target distribution analyses.

M1.justification: The special-token confidence mechanism, probe-based calibration targets, combined calibration/SFT loss, LoRA training, weighted self-consistency, and early-stopping procedure remain unchanged. Specifying the probe's mean squared error loss adds implementation information without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate open-ended generation and cross-domain calibration on TriviaQA/SciQ and test-time scaling on MathQA/ARC_Challenge. The new target-distribution plots concern existing datasets and backbones.

E2.justification: The six calibration comparators remain Seq. Likelihood, Platt Scaling, P(True), Verbal, Apricot, and ActCab. SC, ASC, ESC, and the P(True)/Verbal confidence-based variants retain their corresponding test-time-scaling comparisons. Baseline descriptions move to Appendix A.3.

E3.justification: Matched experiments retain their backbones, decoding and correctness rules, metrics, sampling budgets, training hyperparameters, and early-stopping threshold. Newly stated open-ended sample counts are disclosures; omission of the general ECE bin-count statement does not establish a changed evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1 and Figure 6 add confidence-target distribution diagnostics for three backbones on TriviaQA and SciQ. Existing cross-domain analyses, reliability diagrams, and case study remain. The GrACE-Disc, GrACE-Pre, and GrACE-SFT ablations move from Section 4.1 to Appendix B.4 with unchanged results.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports kernel-density estimation of confidence-target distributions, adding a descriptive statistical estimation procedure. Both versions retain averaging over five random seeds and Figure 1's error-bar reporting; no increase in runs or new inferential uncertainty procedure is documented.

E6.justification: All four matched benchmark/ablation tables retain their numerical entries, as do the existing cross-domain and reliability results. V2 adds target-distribution findings and an introductory 1.54% average test-time-scaling accuracy improvement summary consistent with the already reported results.

T1.justification: Equation 3 changes calibration from P(f(y_i)=1 | c_i=p)=p to P(f(y)=1 | x,y,c)=c, adding conditioning on the prompt and response. New Appendix B.2 introduces Equation 9 and argues that fitting bin-accuracy targets minimizes ECE, adding mathematical reasoning beyond merely stating the metric.

C1.justification: The principal claims remain on-the-fly calibrated confidence, domain generalization, and more accurate and efficient test-time scaling. The expanded title and reordered contributions emphasize test-time scaling, which was already a central contribution in v1.

C2.justification: Section 3.2.3 newly explains the loss as promoting the confidence token while suppressing competing tokens. Appendix B interprets the target distributions as supporting discrimination and connects target fitting to calibration. Existing experimental interpretations and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V2 specifies mean squared error for probe training and discloses 2,000 training queries and 1,000 evaluation queries for open-ended generation. Conversely, v1's explicit statement that ECE uses ten bins in all experiments disappears; the retained ten-bin ablation description does not replace that general specification.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Qwen3 technical report and Niculescu-Mizil and Caruana's probability-estimation work. It removes the Plaut et al. multiple-choice softmax discussion and the Kim/Zheng LLM-as-judge discussion and references. The central positioning against post-generation and verbalized confidence methods remains.

P1.justification: The document substantially reorganizes material between the main text and appendices: baseline descriptions and the complete ablation study move out of Section 4, while limitations move before the references. V2 also expands the title, reorganizes contributions, adds an ethics statement, and restructures Appendix B.

P2.justification: V2 changes the body to a two-column layout, rearranges Figure 1 from a horizontal sequence into a compact grid, and adds the six-panel target-distribution figure. Existing figures and tables are resized and repositioned, including relocating the ablation table to the appendix.

improvement.justification: The sample-count and probe-loss disclosures and new target-distribution diagnostics improve transparency. However, Equation 3 changes calibration's conditioning, Appendix B.2 asserts an equivalence between target fitting and ECE minimization without establishing compatible binning or objectives, and the general ECE bin-count specification disappears. These documentation gains coexist with losses of formal and reproducibility clarity, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
